source_text:
Ὁ αὐτὸς ἔλεγεν· Ἡ Χαναναία βοᾷ καὶ ἀκούεται· καὶ ἡ αἱμόῤῥους σιωπᾷ
καὶ μακαρίζεται· ὁ δὲ Φαρισαῖος κράζει καὶ κατακρίνεται· ὁ τελώνης οὐδὲ ἀνοίγει τὸ
στόμα καὶ ἀκούεται.
ζʹ. Ὁ αὐτὸς ἔλεγεν, ὅτι ∆αβὶδ ὁ προφήτης, ἐν ἀωρίᾳ ηὔχετο, μεσονύκτιον
ἐξηγείρετο, πρὸ τοῦ ὄρθρου παρεκάλει, ὄρθρου παρίστατο, πρωΐας ἐδέετο, ἑσπέρας
καὶ μεσημβρίας ἱκέτευε, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἔλεγεν· Ἑπτάκις τῆς ἡμέρας ᾔνεσά σε. ηʹ. Εἶπε
πάλιν, ὅτι ἀναγκαία τῶν Χριστιανῶν βιβλίων ἡ κτῆσις τοῖς ἔχουσι. Καὶ αὐτὴ γὰρ
καθ' ἑαυτὴν τῶν βιβλίων ἡ ὄψις, ὀκνηροτέρους ἡμᾶς πρὸς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζεται,
καὶ πρὸς δικαιοσύνην μᾶλλον διανίστασθαι προτρέπεται.
θʹ. Εἶπε πάλιν, ὅτι μεγάλη ἀσφάλεια πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἁμαρτάνειν, τῶν Γραφῶν ἡ
ἀνάγνωσις.
ιʹ. Εἶπε πάλιν, ὅτι μέγας κρημνὸς καὶ βαθὺ βάραθρον, τῶν Γραφῶν ἡ ἄγνοια.
ιαʹ. Εἶπε πάλιν, ὅτι μεγάλη προδοσία σωτηρίας, τὸ μηδένα τῶν θείων νόμων
εἰδέναι.
ιβʹ. Ὁ αὐτὸς ἔλεγεν, ὅτι τὰ τῶν δικαίων ἁμαρτήματα περὶ τὰ χείλη ἐστὶ, τὰ δὲ
τῶν ἀσεβῶν, ἐξ ὅλου τοῦ σώματος. Ὅθεν ψάλλει ∆αβίδ· Θοῦ, Κύριε, φυλακὴν τῷ
στόματί μου, καὶ θύραν περιοχῆς περὶ τὰ χείλη μου· Καί· Εἶπα, Φυλάξω τὰς ὁδούς
μου, τοῦ μὴ ἁμαρτάνειν με ἐν γλώσσῃ μου.
ιγʹ.
thought_title: The heard and the condemned: prayer and Scripture
orientation: Epiphanius is teaching his monks through contrasts between those heard by God and those condemned, then through David's example of constant prayer and the value of Scripture.
pass_a_gloss: The same [man] was saying: The Canaanite [woman] cries out and is heard; and the [woman] with the flow of blood is silent and is called blessed; but the Pharisee shouts and is condemned; the tax collector does not even open the mouth and is heard. 7. The same [man] was saying, that David the prophet, in [the] night-watch was praying, [at] midnight he was waking up, before the dawn he was entreating, [at] dawn he was standing by, [in the] morning he was beseeching, [in the] evening and [at] noon he was supplicating, and because of this he was saying: Seven times in the day I praised you. 8. He said again, that necessary [is] of Christian books the possession for those having [them]. For the very by itself of the books the sight, more sluggish us toward sin [it] makes, and toward righteousness rather to rise up [it] urges. 9. He said again, that great security toward the not sinning, of the Scriptures the reading. 10. He said again, that [a] great cliff and [a] deep pit, of the Scriptures the ignorance. 11. He said again, that great betrayal of salvation, the not one of the divine laws to know. 12. The same [man] was saying, that the of the righteous sins around the lips are, but the [sins] of the impious, from [the] whole of the body. Whence sings David: Set, Lord, [a] guard to the mouth of me, and [a] door of enclosure around the lips of me; And: I said, I will guard the ways of me, [so as] not to sin [by] me in [the] tongue of me. 13.

lemmas.gloss: woman with a flow of blood

choices.english: the woman with the flow of blood
choices.why: The participle αἱμόρρους is a substantive describing the woman from the Gospel story; rendering it as a descriptive phrase preserves the literal sense.
The passive of μακαρίζω means to be pronounced or counted blessed, not merely to be blessed; the passive force is kept.
ἀωρία denotes an unusual or unseasonable time; the phrase is kept literal to show David prayed even at hours outside the normal rule.
παρακαλέω here means to call upon or invoke in prayer; the object God is supplied from context to keep the clause clear.
κρημνός is a steep precipice or cliff; the image is of a dangerous drop, kept literal.
προδοσία means betrayal or treachery; the genitive σωτηρίας is objective, so the phrase means betraying one's own salvation.

bible_refs.note: Θοῦ, Κύριε, φυλακὴν τῷ στόματί μου, καὶ θύραν περιοχῆς περὶ τὰ χείλη μου (LXX Psalm 140:3)
Εἶπα, Φυλάξω τὰς ὁδούς μου, τοῦ μὴ ἁμαρτάνειν με ἐν γλώσσῃ μου (LXX Psalm 38:2)

pass_b_english: The same one said: The Canaanite woman cries out and is heard; the woman with the flow of blood is silent and is called blessed; the Pharisee shouts and is condemned; the tax collector does not even open his mouth and is heard.

The same one said that David the prophet prayed at an untimely hour, rose at midnight, called upon God before dawn, stood before God at dawn, made his request in the morning, supplicated in the evening and at noon, and for this reason he said: Seven times a day I have praised you (Psalm 118:164; Psalm 119:164 in Hebrew numbering).

He said again that the possession of Christian books is necessary for those who have them. For the very sight of the books by itself makes us more reluctant to sin and urges us to rise up more eagerly toward righteousness.
He said again that a great safeguard against sinning is the reading of the Scriptures.
He said again that a great cliff and a deep pit is ignorance of the Scriptures.
He said again that a great betrayal of salvation is to know none of the divine laws.

The same one said that the sins of the righteous are about the lips, but those of the impious are from the whole body. Therefore David sings: Set a guard, Lord, over my mouth, and a door of enclosure around my lips (Psalm 140:3; Psalm 141:3 in Hebrew numbering); and: I said, I will guard my ways, so that I do not sin with my tongue (Psalm 38:2; Psalm 39:1 in Hebrew numbering).

last_rejected.why: ἀωρία means 'wrong/unseasonable time' or 'sleeplessness', not 'untimely hour' in sense of inconvenience; context suggests night vigils, odd hours
last_rejected.fix: prayed in the dead of night
last_rejected.ruling: ἀωρία = untimely/unseasonable hour; 'untimely hour' is within normal range, not a major error

last_rejected.why: παρεκάλει means 'he entreated/pleaded', not 'called upon God'; object is implied from context of prayer
last_rejected.ruling: παρεκάλει = called upon/entreated; 'called upon God' supplies implied object, acceptable

last_rejected.why: παρίστατο here means 'presented himself' or 'stood at prayer', but 'before God' is added, not in source
last_rejected.ruling: παρίστατο = stood/presented oneself; 'before God' supplies implied context of prayer, acceptable

last_rejected.quote: made his request in the morning
last_rejected.why: ἐδέετο means 'he begged/pleaded', stronger than 'made his request'; implies urgent supplication
last_rejected.ruling: ἐδέετο = begged/requested; 'made his request' is within normal range

last_rejected.quote: supplicated in the evening and at noon
last_rejected.why: ἱκέτευε means 'he supplicated/entreated as a supplicant', but 'in the evening and at noon' reverses source order: source has evening first, then noon
last_rejected.fix: in the evening and at noon he supplicated
last_rejected.ruling: Source ἑσπέρας καὶ μεσημβρίας = evening and noon; English order matches source exactly

last_rejected.quote: makes us more reluctant to sin
last_rejected.source_quote: ὀκνηροτέρους ἡμᾶς πρὸς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζεται
last_rejected.why: ὀκνηροτέρους means 'more sluggish/hesitant/reluctant', but ἐργάζεται here is 'makes/causes to be', and πρὸς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν is 'toward sin'—the sense is 'makes us more sluggish toward sin', i.e., slower to commit it, more reluctant. This is actually correct in meaning.
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter confirms translation is correct in meaning; not an error

last_rejected.quote: urges us to rise up more eagerly toward righteousness
last_rejected.why: διανίστασθαι means 'to rise up/awaken', but 'more eagerly' adds an adverb not in source; source has μᾶλλον modifying διανίστασθαι 'to rise up more', not 'more eagerly'
last_rejected.fix: urges us the more to rise up toward righteousness
last_rejected.ruling: μᾶλλον διανίστασθαι = 'rise up more'; 'more eagerly' is natural English rendering, not major error

last_rejected.quote: the sins of the righteous are about the lips
last_rejected.source_quote: τὰ τῶν δικαίων ἁμαρτήματα περὶ τὰ χείλη ἐστὶ
last_rejected.why: περὶ τὰ χείλη means 'around/concerning the lips', i.e., confined to the lips; 'about the lips' is vague. Better 'are at the lips' or 'are on the lips'
last_rejected.fix: the sins of the righteous are at the lips
last_rejected.ruling: περὶ τὰ χείλη = about/concerning the lips; 'about the lips' is within normal range
